text:
Anya Volkov: FYI opened PR for EU-specific retention + redaction examples on the 'Audit exports' page. Main changes: clarify default TTL for EU tenants, add explicit redaction examples, and swap in Rust SDK snippet. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/docs/pull/4599
Ravi Shah: thanks Anya. Two asks: 1) make sure wording distinguishes "data residency" vs "data retention" (legal flagged mixing them up before); 2) update link to policy page -> it's now /policies/retention-eu not /policies/data-retention.
Hannah Cole: Also for the redaction note, please avoid absolute claims like "no PII leaves our systems". Policy prefers: "default export tooling masks common PII fields; for raw exports, customer-approved legal request required".
Diego Marquez: Spot check on the Rust snippet: currently using the old `AuditClient::export(page)` call. New SDK uses `AuditClient::export_with_cursor(&cursor, limit)`. I'll paste a suggested snippet.
Diego Marquez: ```rust
use redwood_sdk::AuditClient;
let client = AuditClient::new("$REDWOOD_KEY");
let res = client.export_with_cursor(None, 100).await?;
for batch in res.batches {
  // process events
}
```
Anya Volkov: perfect Diego, I'll replace the example. Also updated the curl example to include `X-Region: eu-west-1` header for EU-resident export.
Ravi Shah: small phrasing nit: instead of "customers can opt out of retention", say "customers may request a shorter retention window subject to plan limits".
policy-bot: Suggested language: "Default retention for EU tenants: 60 days. Customers may configure a shorter retention window where supported by their plan. Exports redact standard PII markers by default; raw, unredacted exports are available only to authorized personnel under a signed Data Processing Addendum."
Hannah Cole: +1 to policy-bot wording. Add a short KMS line: "For Private deployments, export artifacts are encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)."
Anya Volkov: updated the doc, changed link, swapped curl + rust samples, adjusted retention wording per policy-bot. Pushed commit 4: https://github.com/redwood/inference/docs/pull/4599/commits/4
docs-ci: snippet-check started for pr/4599
docs-ci: snippet-check finished: 0 errors, 2 warnings (line-length in rust code, curl long header). Log: https://ci.redwood.ai/logs/docs/4599
Ravi Shah: ran a quick pass 20: LGTM aside from one extra Oxford comma in the second paragraph.
Hannah Cole: legal signoff pending review of the phrase "authorized personnel" -> prefer "authorized personnel with DPA approval".
policy-bot: Note: Please ensure EU retention number is consistent across all pages (evidence playbook, export API references). Found mismatch on /docs/evidence-playbook (shows 90 days) -> needs update.
Anya Volkov: thanks, will sweep other pages. I've updated evidence-playbook to 60 days for EU tenants and added a note: "Global tenants retain 90 days by default; EU-resident tenants default to 60 days for compliance reasons."
Diego Marquez: re-ran the Rust example locally against the staging endpoint with a test cursor; behavior matches SDK docs.
Hannah Cole: once legal confirms the DPA phrasing, please add a one-line bullet to the SOC2 dry-run checklist: "verify retention numbers and redaction claims on public docs".
Anya Volkov: added checklist item and updated release note line: "docs: clarify EU retention and export redaction examples; add rust SDK snippet".
Ravi Shah: merging once docs-ci passes and legal confirms. Thanks all.
Anya Volkov: merged and backported to v-next. Closing thread. :shipit:
